jobs.description:
Introduction

Welcome to Gallagher - a global community of people who bring bold ideas, deep expertise, and a shared commitment to doing what’s right. We help clients navigate complexity with confidence by empowering businesses, communities, and individuals to thrive. At Gallagher, you’ll find more than a job; you’ll find a culture built on trust, driven by collaboration, and sustained by the belief that we’re better together. Whether you join us in a client-facing role or as part of our brokerage division, our benefits and HR consulting division, or our corporate team, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, make an impact, and be part of something bigger. Experience a workplace where you’re encouraged to be yourself, supported to succeed, and inspired to keep learning. That’s what it means to live The Gallagher Way.

Overview

The Security Manager, North America is responsible for supporting and executing Gallagher Global Safety & Security programs across North America. The position provides operational leadership for physical security, employee safety, threat and incident management, emergency preparedness, security intelligence, security technology, vendor oversight, and regional risk mitigation.

Reporting to the Senior Regional Security Manager, Americas, the Security Manager translates global and Americas security strategies into consistent and effective regional practices. The position serves as a primary regional point of contact for security matters and partners closely with business leadership, Human Resources, Legal, Real Estate, Technology, Compliance, Business Continuity, local office leadership, the Global Security Response Center, and external security providers.

The Security Manager conducts site risk assessments, coordinates responses to security incidents, supports investigations, oversees local security services, and promotes the consistent application of Gallagher security standards. The position must balance enterprise requirements with applicable federal, state, provincial, and local laws and the operational needs of individual offices and business units.

How You'll Make An Impact

Regional Security Operations

Manage the day-to-day execution of Gallagher Global Safety & Security programs across North America.
Implement global and Americas security standards, procedures, controls, and initiatives at the regional and local levels.
Serve as a primary security advisor and point of contact for North American business and office leadership.
Identify security gaps, evaluate operational risk, and develop practical corrective-action recommendations.
Coordinate regional security activities with the Senior Regional Security Manager, Americas, and applicable GSS program leaders.
Maintain awareness of crime trends, civil unrest, severe weather, natural hazards, regulatory developments, and other conditions that could affect Gallagher personnel, offices, or operations.
Provide timely incident reports, risk updates, operational metrics, and recommendations to GSS leadership.
Maintain regional operating procedures, escalation protocols, emergency contacts, and related security documentation.

Physical Security and Site Risk Management

Conduct physical security risk assessments, site-security reviews, audits, and operational readiness evaluations.
Document vulnerabilities, recommend risk-based corrective actions, and monitor remediation through completion.
Support security planning for new offices, relocations, consolidations, expansions, acquisitions, and office closures.
Partner with Physical Security, Real Estate, Technology, local leadership, property management, and vendors regarding access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, visitor management, duress alarms, and related systems.
Support the implementation and ongoing review of Gallagher minimum physical security standards.
Evaluate local operating conditions and recommend security measures appropriate to the location, business operation, workforce, and identified risk.
Maintain accurate site-security profiles, contact records, assessment results, and supporting documentation.
Assist office leaders with security-related landlord and property-management issues.

Risk, Threat, Intelligence, and Incident Management

Coordinate or support responses to workplace violence concerns, threats, suspicious activity, theft, physical security incidents, employee safety matters, protests, civil unrest, natural hazards, and other disruptive events.
Serve as an in-region escalation point in coordination with the Global Security Response Center and the Senior Regional Security Manager, Americas.
Gather, document, preserve, and communicate relevant incident information using established GSS protocols.
Support threat assessments and security investigations with GSS Threat Management, Human Resources, Legal, Compliance, and other authorized stakeholders.
Recommend proportionate protective measures based on available information, vulnerabilities, and business requirements.
Participate in incident-management and crisis-management calls.
Support the development and testing of emergency response, employee accountability, evacuation, shelter-in-place, and notification procedures.
Conduct or facilitate post-incident reviews and monitor corrective actions through completion.

Travel, Event, and Executive Support

Coordinate with GSS intelligence, travel risk, and executive protection resources regarding elevated-risk travel and events.
Support Gallagher’s Travel Risk Management program.
Support security planning for corporate events, executive visits, leadership meetings, and other significant business activities.
Assist with transportation-security assessments, route considerations, hotel-security reviews, and local provider coordination when required.
Escalate elevated-risk travel or executive-movement concerns to the Senior Regional Security Manager, Americas, and applicable GSS program leaders.
Maintain awareness of country-specific entry, movement, communication, and emergency-response considerations relevant to security support.

Business Partnership and Stakeholder Support

Develop effective working relationships with business leaders, office leadership, Human Resources, Legal, Real Estate, Technology, Compliance, Business Continuity, Communications, and other internal partners.
Translate security risks and technical information into clear, practical recommendations for non-security stakeholders.
Provide localized security support while maintaining alignment with Gallagher enterprise standards.
Promote a consistent, visible, and service-oriented GSS presence while recognizing that each country and office may require individualized attention based on its operating environment, business needs, and risk profile.
Participate in regional business meetings, office planning activities, and security-related projects.
Deliver or coordinate employee security awareness briefings, exercises, communications, and training.
Provide oversight and coordination of regional security vendors, technology providers, and other security-related service partners.
Monitor vendor performance, service delivery, compliance requirements, and adherence to contractual obligations and established standards.

Program Development and Continuous Improvement

Support the continued maturation of Gallagher’s North American security program by identifying emerging risks, monitoring regional trends, evaluating significant incidents, escalating enterprise-level concerns, and recommending improvements to processes, technology, communications, training, reporting, and service delivery.
Track incidents, assessment findings, corrective actions, vendor performance, and regional security-program metrics.
Contribute to regional dashboards, country-risk profiles, risk registers, leadership reports, and program reviews.
Share regional intelligence, lessons learned, and effective local practices with the wider GSS team.
Participate in Americas and global GSS initiatives, exercises, assessments, and special projects.
Help connect North American offices with appropriate GSS expertise, standards, systems, and response capabilities.
Support planning and regional budget development by identifying anticipated security requirements, country-specific costs, and program priorities.

About You

Required:

Bachelor's Degree or equivalent experience and training in related fields required + minimum of 5 years' experience in the field Corporate Safety and Security.
Ability to be on call 24/7 basis as part of a response team for any related emergencies.
Knowledge of life safety systems, electronic security, video and digital recording systems.

Highly Preferred:

Bachelor’s degree in Security Management, Criminal Justice, Emergency Management, Business, International Relations, or a related discipline, or equivalent applicable professional experience.
Five or more years of progressive experience in corporate security, physical security, incident management, law enforcement, military security, emergency management, investigations, or a related risk function.
Experience supporting security operations across multiple offices, states, provinces, or jurisdictions.
Experience conducting physical security assessments and developing practical risk-mitigation recommendations.
Experience coordinating responses to security incidents with business stakeholders and outside agencies.

Experience overseeing contract security providers or other third-party security services.

Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and related business applications.
Ability to travel throughout North America and occasionally internationally.
Ability to support urgent incident response outside normal business hours.

Preferred:

Experience in a multinational, federated, or decentralized corporate environment.
Experience supporting office acquisitions, integrations, relocations, or physical security upgrades.

Experience working with a GSOC, GSRC, or similar security monitoring and incident-coordination function.
Experience developing security awareness programs, exercises, and employee communications.

jobs.description:
About Us

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR
, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.
We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.
We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.

The Role

Strategic Initiatives takes on some of Legora’s most important cross-functional challenges, helping the company deliver major changes and build capabilities as it grows.

You’ll lead the delivery of complex change programs that span business teams, processes and technology. This means understanding what the business needs, getting deep enough into the technical detail to make sound recommendations, and bringing people together to turn decisions into working solutions.

Your first major assignment will be our Workday implementation, partnering closely with the People Tech leader, business stakeholders and implementation partners. Over time, you’ll bring the same approach to other company priorities. Each assignment should leave behind a lasting improvement, clear ownership and teams equipped to carry the work forward.

What You’ll Do

Shape the program. Turn a business objective into clear outcomes, scope, workstreams and an integrated delivery plan. Establish who owns the work, how decisions get made and how success will be measured.
Connect business needs and technical decisions. Understand how teams operate and how changes affect processes, systems and data. Work with specialists to evaluate options, identify downstream consequences and recommend a practical path.
Drive execution across teams. Manage dependencies, competing priorities, risks and decisions across internal teams and external partners. Hold people accountable for commitments, resolve blockers and step into gaps when needed.
Lead the change through adoption. Involve affected teams early, understand what will change for them, and coordinate changes to workflows, responsibilities, communications and training. Follow through until new ways of working are established.
Help leaders make informed decisions. Bring clear recommendations grounded in business impact, cost and risk. Challenge assumptions constructively and escalate issues with options and a point of view.
Make the outcome last. Coordinate testing, business readiness, rollout and stabilization. Plan the handover from the beginning, establish a durable owner and use lessons learned to improve how future programs are delivered.

What You Bring

8+ years of relevant experience in technical program management, business transformation or operations, with a track record of independently leading complex cross-functional change from scoping through implementation and adoption. We welcome other paths that demonstrate equivalent depth and ownership.
Technical fluency: you can understand system interactions, integrations and data flows, question assumptions and work credibly with technical specialists.
Strong business judgment and the ability to get up to speed in unfamiliar areas, understand different teams’ needs and weigh competing priorities.
The ability to build trust and influence senior stakeholders without relying on formal authority, including navigating disagreement and holding difficult conversations.
A practical, hands-on approach. You bring structure to ambiguity, take ownership of outcomes and adapt your approach to what the problem requires.
Experience defining success measures and using evidence to assess whether a change has delivered its intended value.

Nice to Have

Experience delivering Workday or another substantial enterprise-system implementation.
Experience leading change in a rapidly growing, international business.

What’s In It For You

Global collaboration: Partner with teams and clients across Europe, APAC, and North America.
Competitive package: Comprehensive salary, benefits, and tools for success.
Meaningful work: Your efforts shape how thousands of lawyers use AI daily.
In-person environment: Union Square office designed for ambitious builders and company provided lunch daily.

Established nearly two centuries ago, FM is a leading mutual insurance company whose capital, scientific research capability and engineering expertise are solely dedicated to property risk management and the resilience of its policyholder-owners. The Project Manager leads the successful delivery of complex technology and business initiatives. The role serves as a central coordination point among engineering, product, machine-learning, client-facing, operations, and business teams, translating priorities into executable plans and maintaining clear ownership across roadmaps, sprints, releases, development requests, quality assurance, onboarding, and client escalations.

This position is accountable for delivery visibility, disciplined prioritization, dependency management, risk and issue escalation, resource coordination, and stakeholder communication. Engineering roadmaps, releases, and sprint management: Coordinate engineering roadmaps, release schedules, sprint planning, and delivery activities. Establish milestones, clarify priorities, track commitments, identify dependencies, and help teams resolve barriers that could affect scope, timing, quality, or business value.
Development-ticket and inbound-request ownership: Own the intake, documentation, triage, prioritization, assignment, and tracking of development tickets and inbound technical requests. Maintain a clear view of status, decisions, dependencies, service expectations, and required follow-up.
Release quality assurance and validation: Coordinate release readiness, quality-assurance activities, acceptance testing, defect tracking, and post-release validation. Confirm that requirements and acceptance criteria are documented, responsible owners are identified, and unresolved risks are escalated before implementation.
Technical client-channel monitoring and escalation: Monitor designated technical client channels for questions, incidents, patterns, and emerging concerns. Route issues to the appropriate technical or business owner, facilitate timely escalation, document decisions, and maintain communication through resolution.
New-client onboarding support: Coordinate technical work associated with new-client onboarding, including requirements gathering, implementation planning, data and system readiness, issue tracking, stakeholder communication, and handoffs among client, engineering, product, and business teams.
Machine-learning data and model-training coordination: Coordinate contributors supporting machine-learning data preparation, labeling, validation, and model-training activities. Track assignments, dependencies, quality requirements, delivery progress, and decisions in partnership with the appropriate technical owners.
Special-client-request routing: Evaluate, document, and route special client requests to the appropriate product, engineering, machine-learning, operations, or business teams. Ensure ownership, priority, feasibility considerations, decisions, and follow-up actions are clearly recorded.
Portfolio planning and prioritization: Partner with PMO and functional leaders to prioritize initiatives and assess pipeline and readiness. Proactively evaluate the impact of planned changes on business operations, clients, and employees, and manage cross-project dependencies.
Project reporting, risk, and issue management: Maintain project plans, dashboards, decision logs, and status reporting covering milestones, deliverables, resource needs, risks, issues, and dependencies. Communicate project health and escalate matters requiring leadership attention or cross-functional resolution.
Stakeholder alignment and change readiness: Build effective working relationships with sponsors, functional leaders, and cross-functional team members. Create shared understanding of the purpose, approach, expected value, and operational impact of prioritized initiatives.
Standards and continuous improvement: Apply consistent project and change-management practices, support compliance with adopted PMO standards and tools, and share lessons learned and practical improvements across portfolio initiatives.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in business, project management, technology, engineering, insurance, operations, or a related field.
Advanced degree and project or program management certification, such as PMP

Experience

At least five years of experience in project management, program delivery, technology operations, product delivery, or a related discipline.
Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional teams and delivering complex technology or business initiatives with competing priorities and interdependent workstreams.
Experience coordinating engineering roadmaps, sprints, releases, development-ticket workflows, quality assurance, or technical-client support processes.
Experience communicating project health, risks, decisions, and delivery tradeoffs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Experience within a PMO, agile delivery environment, insurance organization, or enterprise setting is preferred.

new_jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Our Mission

You call. You wait. You call again. In every other part of your life, you book in seconds. In healthcare, you’re blocked.

We’re here to give power to the patient.

For nearly 20 years, we’ve built the leading healthcare marketplace - helping tens of millions of people find and book the care they need. Now, we’re going further: building our infrastructure beyond Zocdoc’s marketplace to power access to care wherever patients search, from provider websites and insurance directories to search engines, AI platforms, and more.

Healthcare still lacks something every other major consumer industry takes for granted: a seamless way to go from seeking to getting . We don’t want to own the front door to care; there isn't one. We want to make sure all of those doors open when patients are knocking.

Fixing healthcare starts with fixing access to it. And we're still just getting started.

Your Impact to the Mission

Zocdoc's most important asset is our people. As a Principal Technical Program Manager for Practice Solutions, you will own and drive the most complex, cross-functional technical programs across the business unit, the initiatives that span multiple engineering teams and product domains and that no single team can deliver alone. Practice Solutions powers how healthcare practices run their day to day across every patient access channel: phone, web, marketplace, and partner syndication. That includes Zo, our AI phone assistant, along with our provider directory and booking platform, intake and pre-appointment workflows, calendar and scheduling experiences, and the services that keep availability accurate across channels. You'll operate at the intersection of Engineering, Product, Design, Analytics, and go-to-market leadership to deliver scalable, highly available, multi-tenant SaaS capabilities. You'll bring structure to ambiguity, drive sequencing across teams, surface architectural and operational risk early, and keep the trains running on time, all while raising the bar for how program execution happens across the entire business unit. This is a highly visible role with significant autonomy and influence.

You'll enjoy this role if you are…

Inspired by the opportunity to positively impact the healthcare experience for millions of patients and providers
A platform thinker who instinctively looks beyond individual features to understand how systems connect, scale, and evolve over time
Energized by building structure in ambiguous, high-complexity environments where multiple teams, products, and priorities intersect
Comfortable operating at both 30,000 feet and in the architectural details, able to reason about distributed systems, reliability tradeoffs, and multi-tenant SaaS constraints
Unafraid to drive movement and accountability at every level of the organization, regardless of title or tenure
Calm and decisive in high-stakes situations, especially when sequencing work across teams with shared platform dependencies
A strong influencer who can align engineering leaders, product leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders around shared outcomes even when ownership boundaries are unclear
A believer that diverse and inclusive teams and cultures are non-negotiable

Your day to day is…

Organizing and driving the business unit's planning cadence, coordinating inputs and stakeholders across engineering and product and keeping the cycle on track so strategy turns into a clear, committed, sequenced roadmap
Leading large, multi-quarter platform initiatives that span the Practice Solutions product scope, keeping each part on schedule and the whole program moving
Translating high-level business and product goals into structured program plans with clear sequencing, milestones, dependencies, and measurable outcomes
Building the reporting and transparency that give leadership a clear, honest view of status, dependencies, and risk
Partnering closely with senior engineering leaders to anticipate architectural and operational risks before they surface in production
Digging into technical issues at the seams between teams, triaging, framing the problem clearly, and pulling the right architects and engineers together to solve it
Surfacing tradeoffs between speed, scope, reliability, and technical debt, and facilitating clear, well-reasoned decisions at the right level
Clarifying ownership boundaries and reducing cross-team friction where systems, incentives, or customer journeys overlap
Establishing and refining lightweight mechanisms that improve transparency, accountability, and long-term platform health
Communicating program status, risks, and key decisions clearly to executive stakeholders and business unit leadership

You'll be successful in this role if you have…

A strong bias to action and an ownership mentality
8+ years in Technical Program Management, Engineering Program Management, or a similar technical leadership role
A track record delivering large-scale, cross-functional initiatives in a product-led SaaS environment
A strong understanding of distributed systems, cloud architectures (AWS or equivalent), and event-driven systems
Demonstrated ability to reason about architectural tradeoffs without owning implementation, and enough technical depth to hold your own in a room full of senior engineers
Experience driving programs that span multiple engineering teams with shared platform dependencies
The confidence to drive accountability and momentum across all levels of an organization without relying on formal authority
Excellent communication skills, including clear written status and risk framing for both engineers and executives
A Bachelor's degree in a technical field (e.g., Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems) or equivalent practical experience
Experience in healthcare or another regulated, multi-tenant domain is a plus
Humility. You believe in treating all people with dignity and respect, regardless of title or tenure, and you approach tough conversations with empathy

Benefits

Flexible, hybrid work environment at our convenient Soho location
Unlimited Vacation
100% paid employee health benefit options (including medical, dental, and vision)
Commuter Benefits
401(k) with employer funded match
Corporate wellness program with Wellhub
Sabbatical leave (for employees with 5+ years of service)
Competitive paid parental leave and fertility/family planning reimbursement
Cell phone reimbursement
Catered lunch everyday along with beverages and snacks
Employee Resource Groups and ZocClubs to promote shared community and belonging

Zocdoc is the country’s leading digital health marketplace that helps patients easily find and book the care they need. Each month, millions of patients use our free service to find nearby, in-network providers, compare choices based on verified patient reviews, and instantly book in-person or video visits online. Providers participate in Zocdoc’s Marketplace to reach new patients to grow their practice, fill their last-minute openings, and deliver a better healthcare experience. Founded in 2007 with a mission to give power to the patient, our work each day in pursuit of that mission is guided by our six core values. Zocdoc is a mission-driven organization dedicated to building teams as diverse as the patients and providers we aim to serve. new_jobs.description:
Description

The Amazon Aviation Security (AvSec) team is seeking an enthusiastic AvSec Manager to provide leadership, and oversight for Amazon Air’s (AIR) cargo transportation business. The AvSec Manager will be responsible for defining and driving new initiatives for the transportation supply chain involving Amazon owned and third-party (3P) delivery methods. This includes independently determining risk-based security standards, exercising discretion in interpreting and applying airport and federal regulations, and making decisions regarding compliance approaches and standardized processes. The AvSec Manager serves as the interface between AIR and AvSec leadership, and will be responsible for exercising independent judgment in identifying, reporting, and leading the correction of non-compliances and deficiencies. The successful candidate will serve as a point of contact for regulatory engagement, lead the correction of non-compliance with established security policies and procedures, and develop and improve processes to ensure operational integrity, owning goals and performance targets for their respective region.

The AvSec Manager supports the AIR operation program as the subject matter expert on interpreting, implementing, and validating security requirements, to ensure associates, 3P vendors, visitors, and assets (people, property, and data) are secure and the organization is prepared to properly respond to various security related incidents. The candidate must have a demonstrated ability to exercise independent judgement, utilize their security expertise and management strength to challenge conventional wisdom, think strategically, and communicate effectively.

Key job responsibilities

The AvSec Manager’s responsibilities include prioritizing team resources and tasks in order to meet AvSec’s targets and goals in an ambiguous environment. This position will lead the business to meet aviation security best practices, regulatory compliance, serving as a subject matter expert in aviation security. This position has a key role in hiring and developing the right workforce strategy to meet long-term process targets.

The AvSec Manager’s responsibilities also include identifying and analyzing gaps in compliance with security procedures and regulatory standards, physical security design standards and policies and leading Security Management Systems (SeMS) processes for risk mitigation. Additional responsibilities include developing new and evaluating existing security standards by establishing workflows, Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and operational excellence mechanisms to ensure customer outcomes are data driven, measured and validated.

This is a new and evolving business operation, and AvSec is looking for someone who can introduce best practices and grow as the team’s scale and scope expand.

Additional Responsibilities Include

Set and clarify requirements and expectations with associates and leadership at each facility.
Create security and quality initiatives that continuously improve processes and mitigate deficiencies.
Provide job-specific training to associates and oversee staffing qualifications and ensure required levels are maintained.
Work closely with site leaders and support staff to ensure on-going support for AIR security initiatives and policies.
Work closely with AIR regional leadership and 3P service providers.
Manage timely, ethical, and professional investigations into security incidents and violations.
Serve as Amazon’s representative for Transportation Security Administration (TSA) inspections and inquiries; investigate allegations of regulatory violations and mitigate regulatory enforcement.
Utilize Security Management Systems (SeMS) to identify the root cause for failures and develop mitigating actions to reduce risk.
Conduct visits, assessments, and audits of processes and records.
Implement security and shrinkage control programs to protect assets from loss due to internal/external theft and operational issues.
This role covers a 24/7 operation and you must be able to work all shifts, including nights, weekends and holidays shifts as necessary.

The Span of Authority for this role includes oversite of a single facility within a geographic region. This will include the hiring and development of team members, supporting operational leadership, managing difficult problems, mitigating immediate risks and deciding if escalation is required.

Eligibility Qualifications

This role is regulated by the TSA and is subject to requirements imposed by the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) because the role will require access to U.S. CBP-regulated areas. Successful candidates must therefore complete all screenings prescribed by the TSA and the U.S. CBP.
Individuals hired into this position will have unescorted access privileges to airport security identification display areas (SIDA). For this reason, eligibility for this role will be limited to individuals who pass a security screening, as required by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and TSA (as applicable).
This position may be subject to Department of Transportation (DOT) drug and alcohol testing. Federal law requires Amazon to determine an applicant's history of DOT drug and/or alcohol violation(s) or refusal(s) to test before hiring applicant into a safety-sensitive position.
This position requires an employee’s full and unimpaired skills and judgment to safely execute their job duties to ensure the safety and security of Amazon AIR personnel, third-party contractors, Airport personnel, cargo, and equipment. This position is therefore designated as a safety sensitive position and is subject to mandatory pre-employment and, where permitted, post-hire drug testing.

A day in the life

The AvSec Manager will ensure the security of Amazon's associates, assets and data at an AIR Cargo facility. You will lead site compliance with TSA regulations, Amazon Policies and Procedures, and local regulations. A successful candidate will leverage their subject matter expertise to assess brand and regulatory risk factors and evaluate opportunities to improve compliance and mitigate discovered risks. You will use independent judgment to investigate cases that would expose the company to regulatory risk, and make recommendations based on an assessment of the risk. This includes developing and driving engagement strategies for Amazon associates and leaders, to drive compliance. A successful candidate will become a subject matter expert on site security infrastructure, policies and procedures, and regulatory compliance. AvSec is a liaison with any law enforcement or government/regulatory officials that visit the site.

Beyond day-to-day operations, you'll contribute to strategic security initiatives. You'll analyze incident trends to identify systemic issues, participate in regional security planning discussions, provide input on policy development, and help shape AvSec's approach to emerging aviation security challenges. This role provides a pathway to develop strategic thinking skills while maintaining strong tactical execution.

About The Team

The AvSec team is responsible for security, loss prevention, and regulatory compliance at Amazon. The organization is built with four core pillars; Security Management Systems, Programs and Quality Assurance, Security Operations, and Credentialing. The organization is committed to identifying and mitigating risk to people, Amazon assets, Amazon brand and regulatory compliance through the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of best-in-class aviation security procedures, standards and guardrails between which Amazon operates. By supporting our customer teams at fulfillment centers and AIR sites to implement process improvements, mitigate risk, resolve equipment issues, and implement new processes to improve performance, AvSec contributes to safe and secure transportation of air cargo to our customers.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent
Experience handling confidential information
Experience with all Microsoft Office applications
Experience in a combination of the following domains: corporate security management, transportation/supply chain operations or aviation security
3+ years of security-related professional, or 3+ years of security service/loss prevention/asset protection/investigations/law enforcement experience

Preferred Qualifications

Analytical leader experienced in performance based, action and results-oriented management, strong project manager and effective problem solver

new_jobs.description:
The Associated Press is an independent global news organization dedicated to factual reporting. Founded in 1846, AP today remains the most trusted source of fast, accurate, unbiased news in all formats and the essential provider of the technology and services vital to the news business. More than half the world's population sees AP journalism every day.

The Associated Press seeks a  Consumer Product Strategist
 for AP News based in New York City. We are a hybrid environment, with employees on site Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.

About The Role

As a Consumer Product Strategist, you will help AP News better understand its audience and use those insights to shape the future of our digital products and user experience. You will look beyond the numbers to uncover the story of how users discover, experience and engage across web and app platforms, turning those findings into clear, actionable recommendations that inform product strategy, experimentation and long-term growth.

This role sits at the intersection of consumer insights, product strategy and analytics. The ideal candidate is naturally curious about consumers, comfortable digging into data and skilled at communicating what the data means with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

What You'll Do

Analyze how audiences discover, navigate and engage with AP News by building repeatable analyses and dashboards in BigQuery, Looker, Omni and Hex to identify patterns in user behavior, feature adoption, engagement and friction points
Connect behavioral data across journeys, funnels, features and retention to explain not just what is happening, but why
Support tracking implementation in Google Analytics 4 and Google Tag Manager to ensure the right data is captured to answer critical product and business questions
Translate complex product and user data into clear recommendations that inform product priorities, audience growth and monetization decisions
Identify strategic opportunities to improve user journeys, feature design and engagement funnels to deepen loyalty
Development and evaluate product experiments and A/B tests, turning results into actionable product recommendations
Build trusted relationships across product, editorial and technical teams to bring consumer insights into product decisions
Translate business questions into meaningful analysis and clearly communicate what the data means

6sense Product Marketing

Principal Competitive Intelligence Manager

Competitive Intelligence & Win/Loss

Team:
Product Marketing

Reports to:
VP, Product Marketing

Level:
Principal

About The Role

The market we compete in is being redrawn in real time. Point data providers are moving up the stack. Workflow and enrichment tools are repositioning as operating systems. Buyers are assembling their own stacks from components that used to be bought as a platform. Knowing what each competitor shipped last quarter is table stakes — the job is understanding what the pattern means and what we should do about it.

This role owns competitive intelligence and win/loss for 6sense. It sits on the Product Marketing team and exists so that our positioning, our roadmap conversations and our field enablement are built on evidence rather than assumption. You will be the person the company turns to when there is a disagreement about why we win, why we lose, and who we are actually competing against.

This is a senior individual contributor seat. The work is research, synthesis and judgment — and the willingness to tell the company something it would rather not hear, with the evidence to back it up.

What You'll Own

The win/loss program, end to end. Interviews, coding, synthesis and the readouts that go to product and executive leadership. Not administering a program — making it the thing people trust when they disagree.
Competitive positioning and differentiation. The evidence behind our claims about where we are stronger, and the honesty about where we are not. You partner with the pillar PMMs so competitive insight shapes positioning rather than trailing it.
Structural market analysis. How buyers are assembling their stacks, where substitution is happening, which categories are converging, and what that means for us eighteen months out.
Field enablement for competitive situations. Battlecards, objection handling, trap-setting questions and talk tracks that hold up in a live deal rather than in a deck.
Claims discipline for competitive material. Sourcing every competitive number we put in front of a customer, and saying no to the ones we cannot stand behind.
Competitive monitoring and alerting, including ownership of the tooling and of what reaches the field versus what stays internal.
Input to roadmap, pricing and packaging, and analyst relations. Competitive evidence should shape what we build and how we price, not only how we sell.

What You'll Bring

8+ years in competitive intelligence, product marketing or research-heavy go-to-market roles in B2B SaaS.
Hands-on win/loss experience. Designing the program, running the interviews and coding the results — not reading someone else's summary.
The ability to run primary research and be honest about what the data does and does not support. Small samples are useful; presenting them as more than they are is not.
Strong synthesis and writing. An executive should be able to read your analysis and know what to do differently.
Comfort presenting uncomfortable findings to product and executive audiences, and holding them under pushback.
Fluency with the B2B SaaS buyer, ideally in martech, RevTech, sales intelligence or data platforms.
Working knowledge of AI and agentic tooling — enough to evaluate what a competitor has actually shipped versus announced.

Nice to Have

Experience with competitive intelligence and research tooling (Klue, Gong, Dovetail or equivalent).
Analyst relations exposure with Gartner or Forrester.
Background in or adjacent to ABM, intent data, GTM intelligence or revenue platforms.
Experience building a competitive intelligence function rather than inheriting one.

What Success Looks Like

In your first 6–12 months, win/loss is a program leaders act on rather than a report they receive; we know with evidence why we win and lose, by competitor and by segment; the field has competitive material that holds up in a live deal; and every competitive claim we make in market has a source behind it.

Job Description

This role is based in the United Kingdom and as such all normal working days must be carried out in the United Kingdom.

Join us as a Compliance Data Analyst

This is an opportunity to take on a purpose-led role in the Compliance Data Analytics team focused on transforming compliance through data, automation and predictive insight, helping the organisation proactively identify and manage regulatory and conduct risks.
You'll be consulting with our stakeholders to understand their needs and identify suitable data and analytics solutions to meet them along with business challenges in line with our purpose

As a Compliance Data Analyst, you'll develop data-driven insights and analytics solutions that help identify and monitor conduct, compliance and regulatory risks across the organisation. We are seeking an Operations Research Analyst I to provide analytical support to United States Air Force (USAF) organizations. In this role, the analyst will evaluate actual and anticipated operational activities to develop quantitative, data-driven insights that support decision-making across military operations, planning efforts, programs, exercises, and strategic initiatives. The analyst will apply established operations research methodologies, scientific principles, and quantitative techniques to assess complex operational challenges and support mission effectiveness.

The Operations Research Analyst I will participate in analytical studies, modeling and simulation activities, operational assessments, and training support efforts. Working under general supervision, the analyst will contribute technical expertise in data analysis, mathematical modeling, statistical evaluation, and decision support methodologies while supporting larger analytical teams and program objectives.

Key Responsibilities

The contractor shall provide analytical and technical support to USAF operational, strategic, and business functions. Core duties include:

Operations Analysis Support: Analyze actual and forecasted operational activities, processes, and systems to develop quantitative assessments that support informed decision-making and mission planning.
Analytical Study Participation: Assist in planning, scheduling, coordinating, and executing selected phases of analytical studies, operational assessments, training, and evaluation activities.
Modeling and Simulation: Support the development, execution, and refinement of analytical models, simulations, and gaming tools used to evaluate military capabilities, operational concepts, and resource allocation decisions.
Quantitative Analysis: Apply mathematical, statistical, engineering, economic, and operations research techniques, including probability theory, linear programming, optimization methods, decision analysis, and game theory to evaluate complex problems.
Data Collection and Assessment: Gather, organize, validate, and analyze operational and programmatic data to identify trends, measure performance, and support analytical conclusions.
Decision Support Development: Produce analytical reports, presentations, briefings, and recommendations that clearly communicate findings, assumptions, risks, and alternative courses of action to USAF leadership and stakeholders.
Technical Problem Solving: Assist in developing solutions to moderately complex operational and analytical challenges requiring creativity, critical thinking, and technical expertise.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Coordinate with government personnel, operational subject matter experts, engineers, analysts, and program teams to ensure analytical efforts accurately address mission requirements.
Methodology Improvement: Support the development and refinement of analytical methodologies, measurement approaches, and assessment techniques that improve the quality and effectiveness of operational analysis.

Required Qualifications

Education: Bachelor's degree in Operations Research, Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Physics, Computer Science, Economics, Data Science, or a related quantitative discipline.
Analytical Expertise: Working knowledge of operations research principles and quantitative analytical methods.
Technical Skills: Experience applying mathematical and statistical techniques to analyze data and support decision-making.
Modeling and Simulation Knowledge: Familiarity with analytical models, simulations, database applications, or decision-support tools.
Communication Skills: Ability to develop technical reports, presentations, and briefings that clearly communicate analytical findings and recommendations.
Problem-Solving Ability: Demonstrated ability to evaluate complex issues, identify key variables, and develop logical, data-driven solutions.
Software Proficiency: Experience using Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word, as well as statistical or analytical software packages.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting United States Air Force operational, testing, acquisition, logistics, training, or planning organizations.
Experience with modeling and simulation tools, analytical software, data visualization platforms, or programming languages such as Python, R, MATLAB, or similar tools.
Familiarity with military operations analysis, campaign analysis, force structure assessments, or resource optimization studies.
Experience supporting operational exercises, training events, mission analysis, or capability assessments.
Knowledge of Department of Defense analytical processes, operational planning frameworks, and quantitative decision-support methodologies.
Experience working within a multidisciplinary team environment supporting federal or defense-related programs.

new_jobs.description:
The Business Analyst, Real Estate and Construction Data
is responsible for translating complex construction and financial forecasting data into clear, actionable insights while supporting the administration, testing, and continuous improvement of Lucernex and related business systems. This role bridges data, finance, operations, and technology by explaining forecast drivers, variances, risks, and assumptions; maintaining system access, roles, workflows, configurations, and data integrity; coordinating the onboarding and ongoing support of internal and external Lucernex users; and supporting system enhancements through requirements gathering, testing, issue resolution, documentation, and user training. The ideal candidate is a strong communicator and analytical problem-solver with system administration experience and working knowledge of SQL and JavaScript, capable of using AI-enabled tools and Microsoft technologies to improve system functionality, strengthen forecast accuracy, automate processes, and clearly explain the rationale behind the numbers.

What You’ll Do

Forecasting Insights & Analysis

Interpret and synthesize construction and financial forecasting data, including cost, revenue, cash flow, productivity, and schedule impacts.
Identify forecast drivers, trends, risks, and variances, and clearly explain their implications to non-technical audiences.
Support short-term and long-range forecasting cycles, ensuring assumptions are well-documented and understood.
Partner with estimating and project teams to validate inputs, challenge assumptions, and close forecasting gaps.

Data Storytelling & Communication

Translate complex datasets into concise narratives, dashboards, and executive-ready materials.
Prepare clear explanations for forecast changes, gaps, and anomalies, including root-cause analysis.
Present insights to finance, construction leadership, and senior management with confidence and clarity.
Proactively surface insights and recommendations rather than simply reporting results.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Collaborate closely with Finance, Construction, and Estimating teams to align forecasts and assumptions.
Facilitate discussions to resolve discrepancies between financial and operational forecasts.
Ensure consistency in forecasting methodologies and definitions across teams.
AI, Automation & Microsoft Tools
Leverage AI tools, including Microsoft Copilot and other approved solutions, to accelerate analysis and identify trends.
Develop dashboards, reports, and analytical models using Microsoft Excel, Power BI, and Microsoft 365 tools.
Automate recurring analyses and reporting processes to improve efficiency and accuracy.

Lucernex & Systems Administration

Use SQL and JavaScript to query data, build reports, and support configuration of workflows
Routinely monitor data quality and integrity with audits and coordinate coorections with data owners
Support the onboarding and ongoing assistance of internal and external users in Lucernex, including account setup coordination, access validation, orientation, training, issue resolution, and guidance on Lucernex processes, workflows, and controls.
Coordinate and support User Acceptance Testing (UAT) for Lucernex enhancements, system changes, and new workflows, including developing test scenarios, documenting results, identifying issues, and partnering with stakeholders to validate solutions before implementation.
Stay current on emerging AI and analytics capabilities and recommend workflow improvements.

What You’ll Bring

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Engineering, Construction Management, Data Analytics, Economics, or a related field.
3-5+ years of experience in financial forecasting, construction analytics, project controls, or a similar analytical role.
Strong understanding of construction cost drivers, estimating concepts, and financial forecasting principles.
Working knowledge of SQL and JavaScript
Experience administering a system or enterprise platform, including onboarding user access, workflow configuration, and testing
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and experience with Power BI or similar visualization tools.
Experience using AI-enabled analytics tools to support decision-making.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
Experience with Lucernex (Accruent) or similar capital project or cost management system, as well as UAT Testing
Experience in construction, infrastructure, or capital-intensive environment.
Familiarity with ERP systems, project management platforms, or cost control systems.
Experience onboarding and supporting external users in systems, including access coordination, user communication, training, and resolution of account, access, or system issues.
Experience with scenario modeling, sensitivity analysis, or long-range planning.
Demonstrated ability to influence without authority and drive cross-functional alignment.

Key Competencies

Data storytelling and executive communication
Analytical thinking and problem-solving
Attention to detail and data integrity
Cross-functional collaboration
Forecasting and financial acumen
Continuous improvement and curiosity
Responsible and effective use of AI tools

The Opportunity: Customer Success Program Manager

LifeLoop is seeking a Customer Success Program Manager to build the systems and scaled engagement programs that help our customers get more value from our platform, and help our CS team do more without stretching further. This is a newly created, high-impact role designed to evolve how we drive adoption, surface risk early, and engage customers between touchpoints. This role reports to the Sr. Manager of Customer Success.

Our Customer Success Managers work across a complex, multi-product customer base—LifeLoop, iN2L, and Linked Senior—each with its own adoption dynamics, user types, and platform maturity. Currently, CSMs serve as the primary engine for every customer interaction, from strategic relationship work down to reactive engagement questions. That model works, but it limits how much proactive, high-value adoption-based work any one CSM can do.

The Customer Success Program Manager changes that equation. You'll build the adoption programs, usage reporting infrastructure, and customer enablement resources that work between CSM conversations—creating a scalable layer of engagement that surfaces problems earlier, drives behavior change more consistently, and frees our CSMs to focus on the relationships and conversations that matter most.

This is a builder's role. You'll own projects from strategy through execution and collaborate closely with CSMs, Onboarding, Support, and product stakeholders. If you are energized by designing systems that scale, thrive on connecting data to action, and care deeply about the customers behind the metrics, this is the role for you.

To be clear about scope: this is not a product management or customer success management role—it's the layer that turns cross-team signals into scalable strategy. And manual, one-off customer reporting stays with the CSM until our underlying reporting system can deliver it at scale; this role does not take over ad hoc report generation from CSMs.

What can you expect the role to look like:

Data Intelligence & Governance

Sit at the intersection of product usage data, customer interviews, Gong call insights, Salesforce data, and renewal risk signals—using AI to synthesize what's driving or blocking adoption across LifeLoop, iN2L, and Linked Senior and turning those into actionable programs
Test and validate adoption approaches (e.g., structured A/B testing) before translating validated insights into at-scale strategies, playbooks, and tools that CSMs use to drive adoption
Define the health indicators and early warning signals that should trigger CSM outreach

Use validated adoption insights to influence LifeLoop's next “bets,” including signal-backed actions, product roadmap changes, and system and tooling recommendations

Connect customer maturity with adoption frameworks that support customers as they move along the journey toward their goals

Build automated re-engagement sequences for communities affected by high staff turnover, a recurring challenge in the senior living operator space

Collaborate with the Customer Services team (Onboarding, Education & Enablement) to ensure programs align with what customers are learning and experiencing early in their journey

Build and manage a customer peer learning community, where operators can share best practices, surface product tips, and learn from one another
Develop a stronger, more proactive customer champions program that can help carry adoption goals back into their organizations and communities to drive best practices

new_jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
About

Swan is the leading European fintech specialized in embedded banking. A laureate of the French government’s selective year list of tech champions, “French Tech Next 120,” we are quickly expanding across Europe.

Over 100 European companies have already seamlessly integrated banking services such as accounts, cards, and payments into their products through our Banking-as-a-Service platform. This approach, known as “embedded finance”, empowers businesses to elevate their offerings and create new revenue streams — often times tripling their revenue!

Our founders’ vision from the beginning was Simplicity: that anyone with a fintech idea at 2 am can visit our website, start building, and buy themselves a coffee with a self-issued card the very next day. That vision has taken us far.

Following a 38M€ Series B round last September, we have been doubling our headcount and already have over 230 Swanees across offices in Paris, Bordeaux, Berlin, Barcelona, Amsterdam, and Milan! If you’re excited about joining a European fintech adventure, Swan is the way!

To learn more about us:
About Swan
;
Our story
.

Job Description

Swan is looking for a Data Analyst to join our Data team, led by Romain, our VP Data. The team has 9 people across data engineering, analytics engineering and data analysis.

This is a hybrid role. Half of it is being a business partner: you'll work hand in hand with your stakeholders, help them ask the right questions, and turn data into recommendations that shape their decisions.

The other half is making data work better at Swan. As our team has grown, so has the variety in how we build dashboards, define KPIs and document our work. You'll lead the effort to harmonize these practices and bring the team along with you. You'll also run initiatives that help the rest of Swan get more value from data, such as Metabase training and data onboarding for new Swanees.

Think of it as RevOps for data: you'll shape not only what we deliver, but how we work.

✨ Your mission

Your mission has two sides:

Data analysis:

Business partner & project lead: Work hand in hand with your stakeholders to understand their priorities and help them frame the right questions. Lead data projects end to end, from scoping to delivery, and turn analyses into recommendations that shape their decisions.
Owner of your domain's data logic: Make sure the data in your scope reflects how the business really works. Define and maintain KPIs, investigate edge cases, write clear specifications for the modeling logic, and safeguard data quality. When needed, you'll build the dbt models yourself.
Data product manager for your dashboards: Build and maintain the Metabase dashboards and EXCO reports for your domain. Treat them as products: understand how they're used, keep them reliable and relevant, and retire what's no longer needed.

Data Enablement & Operations:

Turn ideas into delivered projects: Take improvement ideas from across the team, including leadership's, and turn them into structured projects with a clear scope, plan and owners. Then carry them through to the end, long after the kick-off energy has faded.
Harmonize how the data team works: Lead internal initiatives that make the team more efficient and consistent, such as a shared dashboard lifecycle, a common process for defining and validating KPIs, the data catalog and its upkeep, and clear documentation of our practices.
Drive adoption and lead change within the team: Consult analysts before designing new standards, build buy-in by involving them early and starting with quick wins, and support the team through the change until the new ways of working become the norm.
Drive AI adoption within the team: Identify where AI can make analysts more effective, from writing SQL to documenting dashboards and answering recurring requests. Test new tools and practices, and help the team adopt the ones that deliver real value.
Help the rest of Swan get value from data: Run internal projects for stakeholders, such as Metabase training and a data onboarding program for new Swanees, so that teams become more autonomous and confident with data.

Preferred Experience

✨ You’re a great match if:

You have 6+ years of experience in data analytics and have worked closely with business stakeholders, ideally non-technical ones.
You're fluent in SQL and at ease with a BI tool such as Metabase.
You've led the adoption of new standards or processes across a team, convincing peers without having authority over them, and can show what changed as a result.
You're pragmatic about process: you know how to keep standards lightweight and focused on what really solves the problem.
You have grit and follow-through: you're the person who turns ideas into reality, keeps momentum when things get slow or messy, and doesn't let a project quietly die.
You enjoy sharing knowledge: training, documentation, onboarding or helping others become autonomous with data.
You handle sensitive or confidential data with care and discretion.
You're excited by a hybrid role, half business partner, half making the team and the company work better with data.
You share our values: team spirit, transparency, ownership, and the humility to keep learning.

✨ Even better if:

You have experience with dbt or building data marts.
You've worked on data catalogs, KPI governance or dashboard lifecycle initiatives.

It’s okay if you don’t tick all the boxes — don’t let imposter syndrome prevent you from applying! 🙌

Swan is committed to providing a caring work environment for all employees, regardless of age, sex, disability, sexual orientation, race, religion, or belief.

About the role:
The Site Security Manager (SSM) serves as the day-to-day manager of a 24/7 datacenter physical security operations team, supporting a client’s datacenter or other critical facility. Reporting to a Campus Security Manager (CSM), the SSM builds a cohesive, high-performing team that delivers a safe, secure, and compliant environment while meeting client expectations. The SSM also collaborates with other campus security leaders to maintain consistent security standards across the campus. Additional responsibilities may include client service and issue resolution, service enhancements, Security Operations Center (SOC) systems maintenance, audit compliance, system monitoring, log and documentation maintenance, and access rights administration. Based on coverage needs, the SSM may be required to support and provide leadership coverage at other assigned sites within the campus/region in addition to their primary site.

What you’ll do:
In this role, the Site Security Manager (SSM) leads the on‑site security team and oversees day‑to‑day security operations within a 24/7 environment. You are responsible for directly managing security personnel, including administrative officers, responders, control room staff, and other security team members, while ensuring consistent staffing coverage and operational continuity.

You partner with local leadership to support recruiting, hiring, onboarding, training, and employee development. This includes coaching and mentoring team members, setting expectations, and managing performance and corrective actions in line with company policy. You also work closely with client leadership across multiple business groups to support site operations.

Operationally, you ensure compliance with security policies, procedures, and standard operating guidelines. You monitor site performance and key metrics, identify risks or security gaps, and drive corrective actions and continuous improvement. You maintain required documentation, logs, and reports, oversee on‑site security systems such as access control, CCTV, and incident management tools, and support audits, inspections, and other compliance activities.

The role requires clear, professional communication with clients and internal partners, including leading meetings and presentations. You escalate significant events and risks as needed, promote safe work practices, handle sensitive information with discretion, and support additional operational needs as they arise.

What you need to apply:
To apply for this role, you should have an associate degree and 6+ years of relevant experience in the security industry, including 3+ years of managing people. Experience leading teams in a security and/or datacenter environment is strongly preferred. You should also have hands‑on experience with security technologies such as CCTV, access control systems, incident management tools, and video surveillance platforms. Strong, practical proficiency with Microsoft Office is expected, as reporting, documentation, and operational tracking are essential parts of the role.

This position is best suited for a proven people leader who is comfortable balancing operational leadership, administrative accountability, and client‑facing responsibilities within a 24/7 security environment.

All applicants must have reliable means of communication and transportation (public or private) to travel to and from work, the legal right to work in the country where the position is located, and proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing in English and a common local language (where applicable).

Applicants must also be able and willing to work a flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, and holidays (such as during emergencies or high‑priority events). Applicants must be able to meet and continue to meet licensing requirements for security officers, as applicable to local, county, and state laws and regulations.

What you’ll get:
We offer more than just a job; we offer the chance to be part of a collaborative and supportive team where your contributions are valued and your growth matters. In this role, you will thrive in a dynamic environment while supporting a prestigious multinational client account. You will gain exposure to global operations and cross-regional collaboration, and you will have access to continuous learning, training programs, and career development opportunities designed to help you succeed.

The extra stuff:
Candidates must be at least 18 years old, legally authorized to work in the job location, and willing to complete the company’s pre‑employment screening, including a background check and drug screening. This role may require evening, overnight, or weekend work, particularly during emergencies or high‑priority events. Work may occur in outdoor or inclement weather or environments requiring protective gear and heightened safety awareness. The role requires the physical ability to sit, stand, and walk for extended periods (up to 12 miles/19 km per shift), climb stairs, and occasionally lift up to 25 pounds (11 kg).

Introduction

Welcome to Gallagher - a global community of people who bring bold ideas, deep expertise, and a shared commitment to doing what’s right. We help clients navigate complexity with confidence by empowering businesses, communities, and individuals to thrive. At Gallagher, you’ll find more than a job; you’ll find a culture built on trust, driven by collaboration, and sustained by the belief that we’re better together. Whether you join us in a client-facing role or as part of our brokerage division, our benefits and HR consulting division, or our corporate team, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, make an impact, and be part of something bigger. Experience a workplace where you’re encouraged to be yourself, supported to succeed, and inspired to keep learning. That’s what it means to live The Gallagher Way.

Overview

The Security Manager, North America is responsible for supporting and executing Gallagher Global Safety & Security programs across North America. The position provides operational leadership for physical security, employee safety, threat and incident management, emergency preparedness, security intelligence, security technology, vendor oversight, and regional risk mitigation.

Reporting to the Senior Regional Security Manager, Americas, the Security Manager translates global and Americas security strategies into consistent and effective regional practices. The position serves as a primary regional point of contact for security matters and partners closely with business leadership, Human Resources, Legal, Real Estate, Technology, Compliance, Business Continuity, local office leadership, the Global Security Response Center, and external security providers.

The Security Manager conducts site risk assessments, coordinates responses to security incidents, supports investigations, oversees local security services, and promotes the consistent application of Gallagher security standards. The position must balance enterprise requirements with applicable federal, state, provincial, and local laws and the operational needs of individual offices and business units.

How You'll Make An Impact

Regional Security Operations

Manage the day-to-day execution of Gallagher Global Safety & Security programs across North America.
Implement global and Americas security standards, procedures, controls, and initiatives at the regional and local levels.
Serve as a primary security advisor and point of contact for North American business and office leadership.
Identify security gaps, evaluate operational risk, and develop practical corrective-action recommendations.
Coordinate regional security activities with the Senior Regional Security Manager, Americas, and applicable GSS program leaders.
Maintain awareness of crime trends, civil unrest, severe weather, natural hazards, regulatory developments, and other conditions that could affect Gallagher personnel, offices, or operations.
Provide timely incident reports, risk updates, operational metrics, and recommendations to GSS leadership.
Maintain regional operating procedures, escalation protocols, emergency contacts, and related security documentation.

Physical Security and Site Risk Management

Conduct physical security risk assessments, site-security reviews, audits, and operational readiness evaluations.
Document vulnerabilities, recommend risk-based corrective actions, and monitor remediation through completion.
Support security planning for new offices, relocations, consolidations, expansions, acquisitions, and office closures.
Partner with Physical Security, Real Estate, Technology, local leadership, property management, and vendors regarding access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, visitor management, duress alarms, and related systems.
Support the implementation and ongoing review of Gallagher minimum physical security standards.
Evaluate local operating conditions and recommend security measures appropriate to the location, business operation, workforce, and identified risk.
Maintain accurate site-security profiles, contact records, assessment results, and supporting documentation.
Assist office leaders with security-related landlord and property-management issues.

Risk, Threat, Intelligence, and Incident Management

Coordinate or support responses to workplace violence concerns, threats, suspicious activity, theft, physical security incidents, employee safety matters, protests, civil unrest, natural hazards, and other disruptive events.
Serve as an in-region escalation point in coordination with the Global Security Response Center and the Senior Regional Security Manager, Americas.
Gather, document, preserve, and communicate relevant incident information using established GSS protocols.
Support threat assessments and security investigations with GSS Threat Management, Human Resources, Legal, Compliance, and other authorized stakeholders.
Recommend proportionate protective measures based on available information, vulnerabilities, and business requirements.
Participate in incident-management and crisis-management calls.
Support the development and testing of emergency response, employee accountability, evacuation, shelter-in-place, and notification procedures.
Conduct or facilitate post-incident reviews and monitor corrective actions through completion.

Travel, Event, and Executive Support

Coordinate with GSS intelligence, travel risk, and executive protection resources regarding elevated-risk travel and events.
Support Gallagher’s Travel Risk Management program.
Support security planning for corporate events, executive visits, leadership meetings, and other significant business activities.
Assist with transportation-security assessments, route considerations, hotel-security reviews, and local provider coordination when required.
Escalate elevated-risk travel or executive-movement concerns to the Senior Regional Security Manager, Americas, and applicable GSS program leaders.
Maintain awareness of country-specific entry, movement, communication, and emergency-response considerations relevant to security support.

Business Partnership and Stakeholder Support

Develop effective working relationships with business leaders, office leadership, Human Resources, Legal, Real Estate, Technology, Compliance, Business Continuity, Communications, and other internal partners.
Translate security risks and technical information into clear, practical recommendations for non-security stakeholders.
Provide localized security support while maintaining alignment with Gallagher enterprise standards.
Promote a consistent, visible, and service-oriented GSS presence while recognizing that each country and office may require individualized attention based on its operating environment, business needs, and risk profile.
Participate in regional business meetings, office planning activities, and security-related projects.
Deliver or coordinate employee security awareness briefings, exercises, communications, and training.
Provide oversight and coordination of regional security vendors, technology providers, and other security-related service partners.
Monitor vendor performance, service delivery, compliance requirements, and adherence to contractual obligations and established standards.

Program Development and Continuous Improvement

Support the continued maturation of Gallagher’s North American security program by identifying emerging risks, monitoring regional trends, evaluating significant incidents, escalating enterprise-level concerns, and recommending improvements to processes, technology, communications, training, reporting, and service delivery.
Track incidents, assessment findings, corrective actions, vendor performance, and regional security-program metrics.
Contribute to regional dashboards, country-risk profiles, risk registers, leadership reports, and program reviews.
Share regional intelligence, lessons learned, and effective local practices with the wider GSS team.
Participate in Americas and global GSS initiatives, exercises, assessments, and special projects.
Help connect North American offices with appropriate GSS expertise, standards, systems, and response capabilities.
Support planning and regional budget development by identifying anticipated security requirements, country-specific costs, and program priorities.

About You

Required:

Bachelor's Degree or equivalent experience and training in related fields required + minimum of 5 years' experience in the field Corporate Safety and Security.
Ability to be on call 24/7 basis as part of a response team for any related emergencies.
Knowledge of life safety systems, electronic security, video and digital recording systems.

Highly Preferred:

Bachelor’s degree in Security Management, Criminal Justice, Emergency Management, Business, International Relations, or a related discipline, or equivalent applicable professional experience.
Five or more years of progressive experience in corporate security, physical security, incident management, law enforcement, military security, emergency management, investigations, or a related risk function.
Experience supporting security operations across multiple offices, states, provinces, or jurisdictions.
Experience conducting physical security assessments and developing practical risk-mitigation recommendations.
Experience coordinating responses to security incidents with business stakeholders and outside agencies.
Working knowledge of access control, video surveillance, intrusion detection, visitor management, alarm monitoring, and related physical security technologies.
Experience overseeing contract security providers or other third-party security services.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to prepare clear incident reports, risk assessments, executive summaries, and operational updates.
Sound judgment and the ability to remain organized during urgent or rapidly evolving incidents.
Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and related business applications.
Ability to travel throughout North America and occasionally internationally.
Ability to support urgent incident response outside normal business hours.

Preferred:

Professional certification such as Certified Protection Professional, Physical Security Professional, Professional Certified Investigator, Certified Emergency Manager, or a comparable credential.
Experience in a multinational, federated, or decentralized corporate environment.
Experience supporting office acquisitions, integrations, relocations, or physical security upgrades.
Familiarity with U.S. and Canadian privacy, surveillance, workplace safety, labor, and emergency-management considerations.
Experience working with a GSOC, GSRC, or similar security monitoring and incident-coordination function.
Experience developing security awareness programs, exercises, and employee communications.
French-language capability is desirable for supporting Canadian operations.

Operational judgment

new_jobs.description:
Summary

The Inventory Data Analyst ensures all locations are properly managing inventory in order to maximize profits and customer service. This position consults company representatives on proper business practices in inventory management and inventory operations including prevention, identification, and disposition of excess inventory. Furthermore, the Inventory Data Analyst is a change agent for promoting new inventory disciplines and culture. In addition, this position will work with cross functional teams to develop new programs to increase operational efficiencies based on studies of past, present, and future data trends.

Job Duties

Enforces Motion's inventory policies and procedures in daily communication with field leadership.
Understands data governance and control distribution of company inventory data points.
Ensures full compliance of audit policies of Obsolescence Program and Physical Inventory / DC Mock Inventory.
Finds new insights and trends which helps identify and solve complicated supply chain problems.
Creates automatic dashboards using current or future tools.
Collaborates with all areas of the supply chain to identify and understand inventory opportunities.
Builds simulation models which forecast outcomes of changes to policies or procedures.
Delivers comprehensive reports in a presentation or written.
Works with the IT Department to enhance current and future inventory systems.
Creates and delivers critical inventory trainings.
Supports excess inventory initiatives.
Participants in the annual inventory business plan.
Performs other duties as assigned.

Education & Experience

Typically requires a bachelor's degree in business, statistics, analytics, or equivalent field work experience. Requires experience managing projects. Background in quantitative thinking and statistical data analysis.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities

Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Access, Excel and SQL.
Strong analytical problem solving skills.
Powerful presentation skills with advanced PowerPoint design knowledge.
Experience with data BI tools. (Tableau, Power BI, Qlik, etc.)

Physical Demands

None required.
